summary: A fresh batch of Pentagon UAP documents released this week focused heavily on sightings of triangular craft near military installations, with witnesses describing low-flying objects that experts say fit a decades-long pattern of "black triangle" reports. The FBI has declined to explain why agents were deployed to investigate one such encounter, raising questions about what prompted the bureau's involvement. Meanwhile, the political landscape shifted as Representative Eric Burlison warned that Democrats plan to shut down UAP oversight committees if they regain the majority after the midterms, adding another layer of uncertainty to disclosure efforts on Capitol Hill. The week also saw journalist Ross Coulthart and former government UAP investigator Luis Elizondo discussing why they believe classified proof of non-human intelligence remains hidden, touching on everything from secret government agreements to alleged hybrid beings. Several archived UAP files dating back to 2021 were added to the public record, though their specific contents and relevance to current investigative efforts remain unclear.
